page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Eating humble pie
title: Eating humble pie
topic: Language to use when you need to stand your ground
description:
Chaos continues at Tip Top Trading. Paper is all over the place and important messages aren't getting through. What can the team do to improve the situation? Paul might have to admit his mistake and ask someone to come back to help out.
This episode focuses on the language that you might use or hear when you need to stand your ground.
phrases: You're the boss and I think the news is better coming from you.
It was your decision in the first place so you need to explain that the situation has changed.

listening_challenge.question: What does Paul tell Denise he has been rethinking?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to the chaotic offices of Tip Top Trading. Now Denise has left the company, the place is a mess and important phone messages are being lost.  What can be done to make things better?  I think we know the answer!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hi. Did anyone take a message for me while I was out?  I'm expecting an important call.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Err… no!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Actually yes Paul. I wrote it on Tom's hand but he washed it off.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Look, good hygiene's very important to me.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hmm. That's not very good is it? What's wrong with writing on a piece of paper?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: We've run out of paper… and pens.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Everything really. Nobody's ordered any stationery or tidied up the office.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's since Denise left.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, maybe I was a bit hasty getting rid of her. It was really just to save money.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, but look, if we can't take messages from possible clients we're going to lose even more money.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes… I suppose you have a point. Maybe I will to have reinstate her.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You mean, get her back?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes Anna, he does. Another way of saying reinstate is he's got to 'reverse his decision'. It means Paul has got to make an awkward call to Denise.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Look Paul, you're going to have to call her and tell her you've made an error… a huge one actually.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: It wasn't that huge? Actually… Anna, you're her good friend, would you like to call her?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Me?! B-b-but I can't.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What a coward! I think it's time to stand your ground Anna. Tell him "You're the boss, I think it's better coming from you", and remind him "it was your decision so you need to explain the situation", and remind him "this is your responsibility". You could suggest he says "I'm sorry, I made a mistake and we would love to have you back."

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK. Do you know what Paul, I think the news is better coming from you… just to make it official.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah Paul, you are the boss after all.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And it was your decision in the first place so you need to explain that the situation has changed.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well, maybe you're right but I can't tell her I'm wrong can I?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Look, just say you're sorry. Tell her you made a mistake and I would love to have you back… we all would.
PaulYes, you're right. I should do it. I'll just have a quick biscuit. Here goes.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hello?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah... h-h-h-ello Denise. It's me… Paul…your boss… your ex-boss from Tip Top Trading.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: How are you… getting on?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Good, good. Actually, I've been rethinking our staffing situation in the office…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: And…well… I'm sorry Denise… I… miscalculated my staffing numbers.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You mean you made a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well, I suppose so. So... I would love to have you back in the office as soon as possible. What do you say?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmm, let me think about it… hmmm… errr… well… hmmm…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What will Denise decide? It was a hard phone call for Paul to make, but not one Anna should have made as it wasn't her mistake. She stood her ground with Paul and used the following phrases:
You're the boss and I think the news is better coming from you.
It was your decision in the first place so you need to explain that the situation has changed.
This is your responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And here is a reminder of the phrases Paul used to try and apologise:
I've been rethinking our staffing situation in the office.
Sorry, I made a mistake. I miscalculated my staffing numbers.
I would love to have you back in the office.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmmm… well… OK then. I'll start back tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh wonderful. I'm so pleased. We'll get your old chair back in position.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Actually Paul, if you want me back I'll need a new chair… and a new phone…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: OK Denise! See you tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: And a pay rise!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: So, is she coming back then?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, first thing tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That's good because we've just had a call from Nice'n'Cheesy – they said nobody returned their call yesterday and that if we don't contact them by the end of tomorrow they will go elsewhere for their plastic grapes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Right, we must act… and act fast.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Let's hope they don't lose that contract. At least with Denise returning to work, things will be a little more organised but for how long? Join us again next time on English at Work. Bye!
